name: Toy Slayer Day 2 Shot
description: Trouble Brewing Day 2 Slayer scenario using a fleshed-out two-day public discussion where India should be the strongest shot.

public_log.msg: Alpha: I’ll open with info. I’m the Washerwoman. I learned that either Charlie or Echo is the Slayer. I know that is not a full clear, but one of Charlie/Echo is the Slayer. I’m just putting that out there early so people can work with it, and so if one of them says something weird later we can remember this.

Bravo: I’m the Investigator. I got that either Hotel or India is the Poisoner. So my mechanical info is on Hotel/India specifically. I don’t think that auto-solves the day, but I do think it means those two need to talk, and I’d rather not execute way outside my pair unless something else gets very compelling.

Charlie: I don’t have a first-night info role, so I’m mostly listening for whether people are consistent and whether the claims fit together. We probably should execute today unless something gets extremely weird. Right now Bravo’s pair is the most concrete thing on the table, but I want to hear from Echo before I lock into anything because Alpha’s info involved Echo too.

Delta: I don’t have opening info either. I agree that Bravo’s Hotel/India pair is the strongest thing so far. Alpha’s thing is also useful but less directly executable. I’d rather not get lost in pure vibes on day one if we don’t have to. So at the moment I am mostly looking at Hotel/India and seeing whether either of them starts trying to muddy the water too aggressively.

Echo: I’m the Fortune Teller. I checked Hotel and India last night and got a YES. I know that by itself doesn’t distinguish which one is the important one, and yes there’s a red herring, but it does overlap with Bravo in a way that feels pretty real. So right now I am not eager to leave both Hotel and India untouched.

Foxtrot: I’m the Saint, so I’d appreciate if we don’t get “fancy” with execution choices. I know that’s annoying to hear on day one, but it matters. Also, on the actual solve, Bravo and Echo are pointing into the same neighborhood, which is more than we usually get on day one. So I really do think we should probably be in Hotel/India.

Golf: I’m the Recluse. Just saying it now because I’d rather not have everybody freak out later if I register weirdly to something. I know that does not directly affect Bravo’s pair here, but it can mess with things in general. Apart from that, I agree with most people that Hotel/India is where the table should probably be looking first.

Hotel: I don’t love how quickly people are treating “two pieces of info touched the same two names” as if that means it’s basically solved. Echo’s result is still a Fortune Teller result, which can be noisy in obvious ways, and Bravo’s result is specifically Poisoner. Those are not the same thing. Also, I think Charlie has been a little bit too comfortable so far for someone who might be the Slayer in Alpha’s info.

India: I think Hotel is making some fair points, even though yes we’re in the same pair. I’m not saying ignore the overlap. I’m saying people are already skipping from “mechanical overlap” to “therefore probably India” in a way that seems premature. Also Charlie being a bit protected by Alpha’s info worries me more than it seems to worry anybody else.

Alpha: Just to add one clarification: my info was Charlie or Echo is the Slayer. Echo has now claimed Fortune Teller. That does not hard-clear Charlie, but it does make Charlie more likely to be the actual Slayer from my perspective. I’m not saying build the whole day around that, just don’t casually throw Charlie away as a random bluff for no reason.

Bravo: I want to repeat the exact structure because I think people are already compressing it incorrectly. I got Hotel or India is the Poisoner. Echo says Hotel and India was a YES. So yes, that means there’s real overlap, but it still leaves multiple worlds: Hotel could be Poisoner and India demon, India could be Poisoner and Echo hit Hotel, etc. I just think those are the two seats we should be comparing.

Charlie: I basically agree with Bravo’s framing. The overlap is good, but it is not a one-step solve. I also think India and Hotel are both spending a noticeable amount of energy on “this is being overstated” rather than on solving inside the pair. That’s not a conviction read, but I notice it. At this point I’d still rather execute in Bravo’s pair than outside it.

Delta: Same. I keep hearing “don’t overstate it,” which is fair in principle, but that can also just be a way to make good info feel less good. Between Hotel and India, India feels a little more focused on undercutting Charlie and the table’s confidence generally. Hotel feels more like generic pushback. Not locking in, just saying that’s my texture read.

Echo: I want to be careful because I know Fortune Teller gets people overexcited. But I also don’t want to pretend my result is meaningless. If Bravo had said two names and I had pinged some unrelated pair, that would be one thing. Instead I hit the exact same two names. I think we are massively overcomplicating it if we drift away from Hotel/India today.

Foxtrot: Yeah, I’m landing in the same place. We always do this thing where day one finally has a reasonably good mechanical lane and then everybody invents reasons to get cute. I don’t want that. Also, because I claimed Saint, please do not do the “maybe execute Foxtrot for info” nonsense if the day gets messy. I’d rather the mess stay in Hotel/India.

Golf: As the Recluse, I obviously dislike any board where weird registration becomes central, so I’m glad it currently isn’t about me. On the actual decision, I think Echo/Bravo overlap is good enough to justify execution in that pair. India feels a bit more agenda-driven to me than Hotel, but I admit that could just be because India is talking more.

Hotel: My problem is still that Charlie is getting treated as mechanically safer than he actually is. Alpha did not hard-confirm Charlie. Alpha said Charlie or Echo. Echo claimed something else, yes, but that still leaves room for bluff chains and poison nonsense. And on me versus India, I don’t think I’ve done anything except point out people are becoming too certain too fast.

India: I really think the table is doing a lazy thing where “India said slow down” becomes “India must be evil.” I am not saying ignore Bravo and Echo. I am saying that if Charlie is bluffing into Alpha’s info and Echo is wrong in any normal Fortune Teller way, this whole day looks embarrassing in retrospect. Between me and Hotel, I would execute Hotel first.
Storyteller: During the night, Alpha died.

Alpha: Well, that is annoying. From the grave, I still want to remind everyone that my info was Charlie or Echo is the Slayer, and Echo hard-claimed Fortune Teller into it. That never proved Charlie, but it did make Charlie the more natural Slayer world. So if India keeps trying to spend today making Charlie feel unusable instead of answering the actual India case, I think that is still meaningful.

Bravo: Okay, Alpha died, which is annoying because that removes the person who had the Charlie/Echo Slayer info. I’m still on my original day one information, though: Hotel or India was the Poisoner. If Hotel was good, that’s bad for me. If Hotel was evil, that gets very bad for India unless something else gets weird.

Charlie: Alpha dying is actually kind of interesting because Alpha was one of the main people making Charlie-versus-Echo feel more concrete. I don’t know if that means much by itself, but it does mean evil maybe cared about that info. I’m still mostly trying to resolve what Hotel’s execution means for Bravo and what Echo got overnight.

Delta: I’m the Undertaker. Hotel was the Poisoner. So unless I’m drunk or poisoned or whatever, Hotel really was the Poisoner. Which means Bravo’s day one pair resolves onto Hotel as the Poisoner specifically. And that means India cannot be explained as “probably just the minion in Bravo’s pair” anymore. That pushes India in the demon direction pretty hard.

Echo: I’m still the Fortune Teller. Last night I checked India and Golf and got another YES. Before people jump: yes, Golf claimed Recluse yesterday, so Golf could be the weird part of that. But the repeated part between my two nights is India. Yesterday was Hotel/India YES. Today was India/Golf YES. The common seat is India.

Foxtrot: That seems pretty bad for India, honestly. Because now it’s not just “Echo hit Hotel and India together once.” It’s “Echo hit India twice, and the other player in the second ping is literally the guy who openly said he is Recluse.” Also Hotel flipping Poisoner is just terrible for India because Bravo’s info is no longer a normal minion explanation for India at all.

Golf: Yeah, I mean, I hate being in the second ping because as soon as I say Recluse everybody uses me as a universal solvent. But in this case I actually think that hurts India more than it helps India. If Echo’s second result is India/Golf yes, then the most natural “Golf made it weird” interpretation still leaves India as the repeated suspicious piece.

India: I think people are again sliding too quickly. Delta could be wrong, poisoned, lying, whatever. Echo’s second yes could just be Golf. The first yes could have been Hotel because Hotel flipped Poisoner. So there is still a perfectly normal world where Echo is just hitting Hotel once and Golf once and I’m the common name by coincidence. That is not impossible.

Alpha: From the dead seat, I still think the shape of this is getting narrower, not wider. My old Charlie-or-Echo Slayer info is not the main solve anymore, but it still matters that India keeps trying to re-litigate Charlie instead of just answering the India case. Between Hotel flipping Poisoner and Echo repeating India, I think town should treat India as the default cash-out unless someone produces a very concrete alternative world.

Bravo: I need to be very explicit here because I think India is trying to reopen a door that mostly closed. My original info was Hotel or India is the Poisoner. Delta says Hotel was the Poisoner. If Delta is true, then my information is resolved, and India is not “the other evil in my pair.”

Delta: Also Alpha dying matters a bit more now that I think about it. Alpha’s info indirectly supported Charlie being the Slayer over Echo, because Echo hard-claimed Fortune Teller into it. Evil killing Alpha removes one of the people who can naturally say “Charlie is probably the Slayer, remember.” I’m not saying that by itself solves it, but it fits a world where India doesn’t like Charlie existing as a live threat.

Echo: Right, and India spent most of yesterday trying to make Charlie feel less usable. Hotel did some of that too, but India really kept returning to it. I know social reads are softer than mechanics, but in this case the social stuff is lining up with the mechanics instead of fighting them. That’s why I’m pretty locked on India at this point.

Foxtrot: Same. And I know we are not supposed to talk as if any one thing is absolute, but this is exactly the kind of spot where town talks itself out of acting because every individual piece has some caveat. Bravo was on Hotel/India. Hotel flipped Poisoner. Echo had India in both pings. Golf publicly pre-explained why the second ping may not even be about Golf. I don’t know what more people want.

Golf: Yeah, the board is just narrowing. If I were town-India, I think my best argument would be “Delta is wrong somehow.” But India’s broader argument has mostly been “there are still abstract worlds,” which is true but not that persuasive. And, again, as much as I dislike saying it, my Recluse claim makes Echo’s second result point more toward India, not less.

India: I mean, my argument is exactly that Delta could be wrong somehow, and that Echo still has normal Fortune Teller ambiguity. I’m not saying it’s a great position for me. I’m saying it’s not a solved position. Also, people keep talking as though Charlie’s existence as some hidden threat means something. Charlie has not actually done anything except be broadly agreeable. That’s part of why I still distrust that slot.
